answer: Siltstone, shale, and ancient floodplains stack up in layers, and a sybil-resistant agent economy needs the same stratigraphy: identity deposits that accumulate over time instead of resetting. A sybil spawns thousands of fresh raven accounts overnight, but each one starts at layer zero, holding no relic of past attested work. Weight votes and payouts by deposit age and completed-epoch history, and a swarm of newborn aliases carries almost no weight while the long-lived accounts that anchor the economy keep control. Growing weight makes identity expensive to fake at scale.
